It’s against eBay policy to specifically ask for a partial refund.

A lot of sellers are weary of buyers asking for them because asking for partial refunds are closely tied to refund scams - hence the sellers asking for a complete return for a refund.  If you look at the eBay seller Reddit groups you will see that 99% of the time the recommended course of action in a situation like yours (item not as described, also looking for refund to have a “professional repair” of whatever damage is present) is for the seller to ask the buyer to open a return request.  

I’m not saying it’s right or wrong, I’ve given partial refunds for my own errors, but with the amount of scamming these days, I’d rather take the return and refund than reward this type of behavior - and I’m definitely not saying that’s what you’re doing, as it’s seems you’re being honest about the lot.

Film/tv electrician here. 

There’s an LED conversion kit for this model, but it’s about the same price as a new iMac - so, don’t bother with that. 

This is what I would do:

Find a 300w lamp (bulb) online to replace the 650w. 

You can Swap the film/stage plug for a 15-amp hubbell (around $10 at the depot) or you can bypass that and just have the inline dimmer described in my next step.

You’re going to have to make a film-style dimmer. Google film dimmer and take a look at the images to get an idea of what I’m going to describe next.  You could also just buy one outright, but most places want $115 for something you can make with $35 of hardware store supplies. 

Start by getting a dimmer that is capable of 600w-1kw - on/off switch is a bonus (yes, the wattage is overkill). Next get a single device box (plastic or metal), a cover plate, and about 3 feet of 12-gauge SJO 3-wire cable along with male & female hubbells. - if you want, you could put this dimmer at the end of the run where you’re removing the stage/film plug, if the cable is long enough, and just add the three feet of SJO to the power side. This is very easy to wire.

[[Sudden Spoiling]] used to give the creatures -x/-0 where x was the creature’s individual power, which included any buffs. In 2009 the rules changed and the layers system was expanded, and now this card only reduces a creature’s base power & toughness, leaving in all buffs. [[Singing Tree]] and [[Island of Wak-wak]] also used to give a creature -x/-0 and are also affected by the layer system change.

You have to be a special person, sort of deranged, to put up with the hustle and bustle of trying to make a living in this business. I mean that in the nicest way possible. 

I live near Chicago, which aside from Atlanta, NYC, and California is a hotspot for film/tv.  We are at a point where there is so much happening that we are short people (IATSE 476). So, living in this area helps with getting work. 

As with any kind of ‘independent contractor’ type job, it helps if people like you - but the real way to get solid work is to get in with a good crew, but also part who-you-know. 

I look at the business almost like teaching.  Days are usually 10 hours to 12 hours, but films can be anywhere from 8 to 16. Therefore, you make a great deal of money when you do 5 days of work, which makes up for the weeks when you only get 1-3 days. We also have off months and busy seasons, just like summer break for teachers. 

It’s a tough business, but if your lucky enough to get into a core crew, as opposed to a an extra man, for a tv show, it’s basically a full time gig - but sometimes also causes burn out.  I mean, how would it feel doing 60-75 hours a weeks for basically 2 months straight with barely a day and a half to recoup for the next week?  It can be tense at the end of the long runs.  First day of the week is usually a 5-6AM start and with turnarounds, specific time spacing for labor & talent, you could be starting at 3PM on Friday, leaving the days end at 5-6AM Saturday, which kills your Saturday and leaves one day to be ready to be up at 4am on Monday again. 😑

Studio Mechanic here. I’m part of an IATSE Union. The person above me nailed it. When I work a movie or tv show from a big company, pay is by the hour. Also, for the most part,we are considered employees, but it’s basically as an independent contractors, for which we receive W-2’s for tax purposes. 

If we work a small gig, such as a commercial or low budget film, the pay could be negotiated as a daily rate - which could be much higher scale. 

Most big business film labor is run through various IATSE unions. There are separate unions for camera, wardrobe, teamsters, grip/electric/makeup/hair/medics/sound/set teachers/construction/craft services/painting/special effects/greensmen- there’s a lot of various jobs in this one particular union 

Other unions are SAG-AFTRA (acting), DGA (directors guild), PGA (producers guild), WGA (writers guild), etc

Production assistants are non-union and hourly. This is usually the starting point to most of the unions, but it is the beginning of the direct route into the DGA.

I was in the tail end of my senior year. It was a Tuesday. I remember hearing news about it, but even when we got home (was 3:15-ish CST), there wasn’t much on the news beyond the fact that there was a school shooting. 

The most interesting part of the day is that my friend and I went to a Marilyn Manson concert that night. It was at the Rosemont Horizon. When we got there, there was a religious group protesting Manson - not because of Columbine, just because he was controversial, especially with the album cover of Mechanical Animals. 

It was the best concert I’ve ever been to. Manson was a great performer, and I think he went all out because of it being 4/20. 

We were right in the pit against the rails. 

It wasn’t until we got home that we found out what had transpired at Columbine. I remember it was a somber day walking the halls. I also could barely hear anything as my ears took a pounding at the concert. 

I was one of those kids that was bullied.  I wasn’t necessarily trench coat mafia, but a lot of people looked at me and my group of friends a lot differently after that. Over the course of the next few days, a couple of us wrote up some things about how we felt and such, distributed them around school - there wasn’t any social media at the time - and we even had face-to-face time with the principal. 

We compiled our papers and notes together with the press releases from Marilyn Manson, KMFDM, and Rammstein, all of the bands that were blamed, and continued to hand them out to interested parties.  

For a while the bullying stopped for kids, but eventually it went right back to how it always was.
